segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The word for "how" in Spanish is "cómo".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How do you think you would say "how are you?" talking informally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿Cómo estás? Because when you ask somebody how they are, you're referring to their state. ¿Cómo estás?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And formally, how would you ask?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And if you are asking more than one person?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, how would you say "where are you?" talking informally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No sé. Good. "I don't know where we are."

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. How would you say "I am here"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say "I want to be here"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. How would you say "I'm going to be here later"? What was the word for "late"? We said we used...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, "I'm going to be here later."

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Voy a estar aquí más tarde.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Voy a estar aquí más tarde.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "Voy" is "I go" or "I'm going". How do you say "you go" or "you are going", speaking informally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, how would you say "where are you going to be?" So, so break it up: "Where are you going to be?"

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Yes. ¿Dónde vas a estar? Where are you going to be?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, let's run through the forms again and let's use the words for emphasis just to practice them. So, "I am" is...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And if we use the word for "you"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Tú estás. Tú estás. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you ask more than one person, "Where do you have to be later?"

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "Do you have..." and we are talking to you plural, which is the same as "they": "do you have"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Tener, good. And we have it as -tain in words like maintain (mantener), contain (contener), sustain (sostener), entertain (entretener), obtain (obtener). That will help us.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So first, we want to build "you guys have" from "tener".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, "where do you have to be later?" to "you" plural. Try it.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Oh sorry, "to be". It's in the... yes.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿Dónde...? And I've forgotten the other one now.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: It's okay. Work it out again.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: There is something we need to add to "tienen" to get this meaning of "have to", and it's not a comfortable translation.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿Dónde tienen que estar más tarde? Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: You might want to say, "He must be here," and you can use this in the same way as you do in English to refer to probability: "Oh, he must be here by now," or something like this. You have the same use in Spanish.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And "must" is the same as "to owe", which is related to "debt". So what was "to owe"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Deber, good. So, "he owes" or "he must"...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Debe. This -e doesn't split, good. Debe.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Debe estar cansado. "They must be tired"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: All together. Don't miss the fun, I mean.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And to get the meaning of "I stay", we say "I remain myself". So how would that sound, "I remain myself"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would "we are staying" or "we remain ourselves" be?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "We are not going to stay because we are very tired." "We are not going to stay because we are very tired."

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So the first bit that needs to command all of our attention is "we are not going"...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No vamos. "We are not going to stay", so "we are not going to remain ourselves"...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. No vamos a quedarnos or no nos vamos a quedar, you could have this as well: no nos vamos a quedar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Porque. "We are very tired", and let's be a masculine or a mixed group. "We are very tired."

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now all together and not from memory, thinking about it again block by block. If you rush it, you will trip, and tripping is very time-consuming.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, "we are not going to remain ourselves" (to stay)...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Well done. No vamos a quedarnos, no nos vamos a quedar porque estamos muy cansados. Very good.
